passages.text: Now Naaman, the commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man in his master’s sight and highly regarded, for through him the LORD had given victory to Aram. And he was a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.
passages.sermon:
Naaman was the commander of the army of the king of Aram.
Naaman was a great man in the eyes of his master.
Naaman was highly regarded.
The LORD gave victory to Aram through Naaman.
Naaman was a mighty man of valor.
Naaman had leprosy.
passages.original: וְ֠נַעֲמָן שַׂר־ צְבָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֜ם הָיָ֣ה אִישׁ֩ גָּד֨וֹל לִפְנֵ֤י אֲדֹנָיו֙ וּנְשֻׂ֣א פָנִ֔ים כִּֽי־ ב֛וֹ נָֽתַן־ יְהוָ֥ה תְּשׁוּעָ֖ה לַאֲרָ֑ם וְהָאִ֗ישׁ הָיָ֛ה גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֖יִל מְצֹרָֽע׃

passages.text: At this time the Arameans had gone out in bands and had taken a young girl from the land of Israel, and she was serving Naaman’s wife.
passages.sermon:
The Arameans were a people who lived near Israel.
At this time, the Arameans sent out raiding parties.
These raiding parties entered the land of Israel.
They captured a young girl from Israel.
The Arameans took the girl away from her home.
The girl became a servant.
She served the wife of Naaman.
Naaman was the commander of the army of the king of Aram.
passages.original: וַאֲרָם֙ יָצְא֣וּ גְדוּדִ֔ים וַיִּשְׁבּ֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נַעֲרָ֣ה קְטַנָּ֑ה וַתְּהִ֕י לִפְנֵ֖י אֵ֥שֶׁת נַעֲמָֽן׃

passages.text: She said to her mistress, “If only my master would go to the prophet who is in Samaria, he would cure him of his leprosy.”
passages.sermon:
A young girl from Israel served Naaman’s wife.
She spoke to her mistress.
She said, “I wish my master would visit the prophet in Samaria.”
She said, “The prophet could heal him of his leprosy.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ גְּבִרְתָּ֔הּ אַחֲלֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י לִפְנֵ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן אָ֛ז יֶאֱסֹ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ מִצָּרַעְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And Naaman went and told his master what the girl from the land of Israel had said.
passages.sermon:
Naaman was a commander in the army of Aram.
Naaman had leprosy.
A young girl from Israel served Naaman’s wife.
The girl spoke about a prophet in Samaria who could heal leprosy.
Naaman went to his master.
Naaman told his master what the girl from Israel had said.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לַאדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר כָּזֹ֤את וְכָזֹאת֙ דִּבְּרָ֣ה הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: “Go now,” said the king of Aram, “and I will send you with a letter to the king of Israel.” So Naaman departed, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten sets of clothing.
passages.sermon:
The king of Aram spoke to Naaman.
The king of Aram said, "Go now."
The king of Aram said, "I will send a letter with you to the king of Israel."
Naaman left.
Naaman took ten talents of silver.
Naaman took six thousand shekels of gold.
Naaman took ten sets of clothing.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָם֙ לֶךְ־ בֹּ֔א וְאֶשְׁלְחָ֥ה סֵ֖פֶר אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּלֶךְ֩ וַיִּקַּ֨ח בְּיָד֜וֹ עֶ֣שֶׂר כִּכְּרֵי־ כֶ֗סֶף וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ זָהָ֔ב וְעֶ֖שֶׂר חֲלִיפ֥וֹת בְּגָדִֽים׃

passages.text: And the letter that he took to the king of Israel stated: “With this letter I am sending my servant Naaman, so that you may cure him of his leprosy.”
passages.sermon:
Naaman was a servant of the king of Aram.
Naaman had leprosy.
The king of Aram wrote a letter.
Naaman took the letter to the king of Israel.
The letter said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you.”
The letter said, “You must cure him of his leprosy.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֵ֣א הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר וְעַתָּ֗ה כְּב֨וֹא הַסֵּ֤פֶר הַזֶּה֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה שָׁלַ֤חְתִּי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ אֶת־ נַעֲמָ֣ן עַבְדִּ֔י וַאֲסַפְתּ֖וֹ מִצָּרַעְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and asked, “Am I God, killing and giving life, that this man expects me to cure a leper? Surely you can see that he is seeking a quarrel with me!”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel read the letter.
He tore his clothes.
He spoke aloud.
He said, “Am I God?
I do not have the power to kill or to give life.
This man sends a leper to me so that I will cure him.
He expects me to heal his servant from leprosy.
You must see that he is looking for a reason to fight with me.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י כִּקְרֹא֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת־ הַסֵּ֜פֶר וַיִּקְרַ֣ע בְּגָדָ֗יו וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַאֱלֹהִ֥ים אָ֙נִי֙ לְהָמִ֣ית וּֽלְהַחֲי֔וֹת כִּֽי־ זֶה֙ שֹׁלֵ֣חַ אֵלַ֔י לֶאֱסֹ֥ף אִ֖ישׁ מִצָּֽרַעְתּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י אַךְ־ דְּעֽוּ־ נָא֙ וּרְא֔וּ כִּֽי־ מִתְאַנֶּ֥ה ה֖וּא לִֽי׃

passages.text: Now when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent a message to the king: “Why have you torn your clothes? Please let the man come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a man of God.
Elisha heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes.
Elisha sent a message to the king.
Elisha asked, “Why have you torn your clothes?”
Elisha said, “Let the man come to me.”
Elisha said, “He will know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ׀ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים כִּֽי־ קָרַ֤ע מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־ בְּגָדָ֔יו וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֥מָּה קָרַ֖עְתָּ בְּגָדֶ֑יךָ יָבֹֽא־ נָ֣א אֵלַ֔י וְיֵדַ֕ע כִּ֛י יֵ֥שׁ נָבִ֖יא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stood at the door of Elisha’s house.
passages.sermon:
Naaman was a commander of the army of Aram.
Naaman had leprosy.
Naaman came to Elisha’s house.
Naaman brought his horses.
Naaman brought his chariots.
Naaman stood at the door of Elisha’s house.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֥א נַעֲמָ֖ן בְּסוּסוֹ וּבְרִכְבּ֑וֹ וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד פֶּֽתַח־ הַבַּ֖יִת לֶאֱלִישָֽׁע׃

passages.text: Then Elisha sent him a messenger, who said, “Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored, and you will be clean.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet in Israel.
Elisha sent a messenger to Naaman.
The messenger spoke to Naaman.
The messenger said, "Go to the Jordan River."
"Wash yourself seven times in the Jordan."
"Your flesh will be restored."
"You will be clean."
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו אֱלִישָׁ֖ע מַלְאָ֣ךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר הָל֗וֹךְ וְרָחַצְתָּ֤ שֶֽׁבַע־ פְּעָמִים֙ בַּיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וְיָשֹׁ֧ב בְּשָׂרְךָ֛ לְךָ֖ וּטְהָֽר׃

passages.text: But Naaman went away angry, saying, “I thought that he would surely come out, stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the spot to cure my leprosy.
passages.sermon:
Naaman was a commander from Aram.
Naaman had leprosy.
Naaman became angry.
Naaman turned and left.
Naaman said, “I thought Elisha would come out to me.
I thought Elisha would stand before me.
I thought Elisha would call on the name of the LORD his God.
I thought Elisha would wave his hand over the place of my disease.
I thought Elisha would cure my leprosy.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְצֹ֥ף נַעֲמָ֖ן וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הִנֵּ֨ה אָמַ֜רְתִּי אֵלַ֣י׀ יֵצֵ֣א יָצ֗וֹא וְעָמַד֙ וְקָרָא֙ בְּשֵׁם־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו וְהֵנִ֥יף יָד֛וֹ אֶל־ הַמָּק֖וֹם וְאָסַ֥ף הַמְּצֹרָֽע׃

passages.text: Are not the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not have washed in them and been cleansed?” So he turned and went away in a rage.
passages.sermon:
Naaman was a commander from Aram.
He had leprosy.
He spoke with anger.
He said, “The Abanah and Pharpar are rivers in Damascus.
They are better than all the waters of Israel.
I could have washed in those rivers.
I could have been cleansed there.”
Naaman turned away.
He left in a rage.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֡א טוֹב֩ אֲבָנָה וּפַרְפַּ֜ר נַהֲר֣וֹת דַּמֶּ֗שֶׂק מִכֹּל֙ מֵימֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֲלֹֽא־ אֶרְחַ֥ץ בָּהֶ֖ם וְטָהָ֑רְתִּי וַיִּ֖פֶן וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּחֵמָֽה׃

passages.text: Naaman’s servants, however, approached him and said, “My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, ‘Wash and be cleansed’?”
passages.sermon:
Naaman was a commander in the army of Aram.
Naaman had leprosy.
Naaman’s servants came near to him.
They spoke to Naaman.
They said, “My father, the prophet spoke a great thing to you.
If the prophet had told you to do something great, you would have done it.
Now he only said to you, ‘Wash and be clean.’
How much more should you do it?”
passages.original: וַיִּגְּשׁ֣וּ עֲבָדָיו֮ וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אֵלָיו֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אָבִי֙ דָּבָ֣ר גָּד֗וֹל הַנָּבִ֛יא דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ הֲל֣וֹא תַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְאַ֛ף כִּֽי־ אָמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ רְחַ֥ץ וּטְהָֽר׃

passages.text: So Naaman went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored and became like that of a little child, and he was clean.
passages.sermon:
Naaman was a commander of the army of Aram.
Naaman had leprosy.
Naaman went down to the Jordan River.
Naaman dipped himself in the water seven times.
He did this because the man of God told him to do it.
Naaman’s flesh became healthy again.
His skin became like the skin of a young boy.
Naaman was healed and made clean.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֗רֶד וַיִּטְבֹּ֤ל בַּיַּרְדֵּן֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים כִּדְבַ֖ר אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיָּ֣שָׁב בְּשָׂר֗וֹ כִּבְשַׂ֛ר נַ֥עַר קָטֹ֖ן וַיִּטְהָֽר׃

passages.text: Then Naaman and all his attendants went back to the man of God, stood before him, and declared, “Now I know for sure that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. So please accept a gift from your servant.”
passages.sermon:
Naaman was a commander of the army of Aram.
He had been healed of leprosy by the prophet Elisha in Israel.
Naaman returned to the man of God.
All his attendants went with him.
Naaman came and stood before Elisha.
Naaman spoke to Elisha.
Naaman said, “Now I know there is no God in all the earth except in Israel.”
Naaman said, “Please accept a gift from your servant.”
passages.original: וַיָּשָׁב֩ אֶל־ אִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים ה֣וּא וְכָֽל־ מַחֲנֵ֗הוּ וַיָּבֹא֮ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד לְפָנָיו֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה־ נָ֤א יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּכָל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֖י אִם־ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֛ה קַח־ נָ֥א בְרָכָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ת עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: But Elisha replied, “As surely as the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it.” And although Naaman urged him to accept it, he refused.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet and a man of God.
Naaman offered Elisha a gift.
Elisha answered Naaman.
Elisha said, “As surely as the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it.”
Naaman urged Elisha to take the gift.
Elisha refused to accept it.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חַי־ יְהוָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ עָמַ֥דְתִּי לְפָנָ֖יו אִם־ אֶקָּ֑ח וַיִּפְצַר־ בּ֥וֹ לָקַ֖חַת וַיְמָאֵֽן׃

passages.text: “If you will not,” said Naaman, “please let me, your servant, be given as much soil as a pair of mules can carry. For your servant will never again make a burnt offering or a sacrifice to any other god but the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Naaman was the commander of the army of Aram.
Naaman had just been healed by the God of Israel.
Naaman spoke to Elisha, the man of God.
Naaman said, “If you will not accept my gift, please let me, your servant, have some soil from Israel.
Let me take as much soil as two mules can carry.
I am your servant.
I will never again offer a burnt offering to any other god.
I will never again sacrifice to any other god.
I will only offer sacrifices to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ נַעֲמָן֒ וָלֹ֕א יֻתַּן־ נָ֣א לְעַבְדְּךָ֔ מַשָּׂ֥א צֶֽמֶד־ פְּרָדִ֖ים אֲדָמָ֑ה כִּ֡י לֽוֹא־ יַעֲשֶׂה֩ ע֨וֹד עַבְדְּךָ֜ עֹלָ֤ה וָזֶ֙בַח֙ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים כִּ֖י אִם־ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Yet may the LORD forgive your servant this one thing: When my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my arm, and I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, may the LORD forgive your servant in this matter.”
passages.sermon:
Naaman was the commander of the army of Aram.
Naaman spoke to Elisha, the prophet of the LORD.
Naaman had just been healed by the LORD through Elisha.
Naaman said, “May the LORD forgive your servant for this one thing.”
Naaman’s master, the king of Aram, sometimes goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship there.
My master leans on my arm when he bows down in the temple of Rimmon.
When my master bows, I must also bow in the temple of Rimmon.
When I bow in the temple of Rimmon, may the LORD forgive your servant for this matter.
passages.original: לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה יִסְלַ֥ח יְהוָ֖ה לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ בְּב֣וֹא אֲדֹנִ֣י בֵית־ רִמּוֹן֩ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֨ת שָׁ֜מָּה וְה֣וּא׀ נִשְׁעָ֣ן עַל־ יָדִ֗י וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֵ֙יתִי֙ בֵּ֣ית רִמֹּ֔ן בְּהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָ֙תִי֙ בֵּ֣ית רִמֹּ֔ן יִסְלַח־ נא יְהוָ֥ה לְעַבְדְּךָ֖ בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: “Go in peace,” said Elisha. But after Naaman had traveled a short distance, Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, “Look, my master has spared this Aramean, Naaman, while not accepting what he brought. As surely as the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something from him.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet and a man of God.
Naaman was an Aramean.
Gehazi was the servant of Elisha.
Elisha said to Naaman, “Go in peace.”
Naaman left Elisha and traveled a short distance.
Gehazi spoke after Naaman left.
Gehazi said, “My master has spared Naaman the Aramean.”
Gehazi said, “My master did not accept what Naaman brought.”
Gehazi said, “As surely as the LORD lives, I will run after Naaman.”
Gehazi said, “I will get something from him.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ לֵ֣ךְ לְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ כִּבְרַת־ אָֽרֶץ׃ס וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י נַעַר֮ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִים֒ הִנֵּ֣ה׀ חָשַׂ֣ךְ אֲדֹנִ֗י אֶֽת־ נַעֲמָ֤ן הָֽאֲרַמִּי֙ הַזֶּ֔ה מִקַּ֥חַת מִיָּד֖וֹ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ הֵבִ֑יא חַי־ יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־ אִם־ רַ֣צְתִּי אַחֲרָ֔יו וְלָקַחְתִּ֥י מֵאִתּ֖וֹ מְאֽוּמָה׃

passages.text: So Gehazi pursued Naaman. And when Naaman saw him running toward him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and asked, “Is everything all right?”
passages.sermon:
Gehazi was the servant of Elisha, the man of God.
Naaman was an Aramean who had just been healed by Elisha.
Gehazi ran after Naaman.
Naaman saw Gehazi running toward him.
Naaman got down from his chariot.
Naaman went to meet Gehazi.
Naaman asked Gehazi, “Is everything all right?”
passages.original: וַיִּרְדֹּ֥ף גֵּיחֲזִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֣י נַֽעֲמָ֑ן וַיִּרְאֶ֤ה נַֽעֲמָן֙ רָ֣ץ אַחֲרָ֔יו וַיִּפֹּ֞ל מֵעַ֧ל הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֛ה לִקְרָאת֖וֹ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הֲשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: “Everything is all right,” Gehazi replied. “My master has sent me to say, ‘I have just now discovered that two young men from the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two sets of clothing.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Gehazi was the servant of Elisha, the man of God.
Naaman was an Aramean whom Elisha had just healed.
Naaman had offered gifts to Elisha, but Elisha refused them.
Gehazi went after Naaman to ask for something from him.
Naaman saw Gehazi coming and asked if everything was all right.
Gehazi answered, “Everything is all right.”
Gehazi said, “My master has sent me.”
Gehazi said, “He told me to say this.”
Gehazi said, “Two young men have just come to me.”
Gehazi said, “They are from the hill country of Ephraim.”
Gehazi said, “They are sons of the prophets.”
Gehazi said, “Please give them a talent of silver.”
Gehazi said, “Please give them two sets of clothing.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ שָׁל֗וֹם אֲדֹנִי֮ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי לֵאמֹר֒ הִנֵּ֣ה עַתָּ֡ה זֶ֠ה בָּ֣אוּ אֵלַ֧י שְׁנֵֽי־ נְעָרִ֛ים מֵהַ֥ר אֶפְרַ֖יִם מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים תְּנָה־ נָּ֤א לָהֶם֙ כִּכַּר־ כֶּ֔סֶף וּשְׁתֵּ֖י חֲלִפ֥וֹת בְּגָדִֽים׃

passages.text: But Naaman insisted, “Please, take two talents.” And he urged Gehazi to accept them. Then he tied up two talents of silver in two bags along with two sets of clothing and gave them to two of his servants, who carried them ahead of Gehazi.
passages.sermon:
Naaman was a commander from Aram.
Naaman spoke to Gehazi.
Naaman said, “Please, take two talents.”
Naaman insisted that Gehazi accept the gifts.
Naaman took two talents of silver.
He put the silver in two bags.
He also took two sets of clothing.
Naaman gave the silver and clothing to two of his servants.
The two servants carried the gifts in front of Gehazi.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר נַעֲמָ֔ן הוֹאֵ֖ל קַ֣ח כִּכָּרָ֑יִם וַיִּפְרָץ־ בּ֗וֹ וַיָּצַר֩ כִּכְּרַ֨יִם כֶּ֜סֶף בִּשְׁנֵ֣י חֲרִטִ֗ים וּשְׁתֵּי֙ חֲלִפ֣וֹת בְּגָדִ֔ים וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶל־ שְׁנֵ֣י נְעָרָ֔יו וַיִּשְׂא֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: When Gehazi came to the hill, he took the gifts from the servants and stored them in the house. Then he dismissed the men, and they departed.
passages.sermon:
Gehazi was Elisha’s servant.
Gehazi came to the hill.
He met the two servants there.
He took the gifts from the servants.
He put the gifts in the house.
He sent the men away.
The men left.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־ הָעֹ֔פֶל וַיִּקַּ֥ח מִיָּדָ֖ם וַיִּפְקֹ֣ד בַּבָּ֑יִת וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ׃

passages.text: When Gehazi went in and stood before his master, Elisha asked him, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Your servant did not go anywhere,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Gehazi was the servant of Elisha.
Gehazi entered and stood before Elisha.
Elisha was his master and a prophet.
Elisha asked Gehazi, "Where have you been?"
Gehazi answered, "Your servant did not go anywhere."
passages.original: וְהוּא־ בָא֙ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אֱלִישָׁ֔ע מֵאָן גֵּחֲזִ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־ הָלַ֥ךְ עַבְדְּךָ֖ אָ֥נֶה וָאָֽנָה׃

passages.text: But Elisha questioned him, “Did not my spirit go with you when the man got down from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to accept money and clothing, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and oxen, menservants and maidservants?
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha spoke to Gehazi.
Elisha said, “My spirit went with you.
I saw when the man got down from his chariot to meet you.
This is not the time to take money.
This is not the time to take clothing.
This is not the time to take olive groves.
This is not the time to take vineyards.
This is not the time to take sheep.
This is not the time to take oxen.
This is not the time to take male servants.
This is not the time to take female servants.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לֹא־ לִבִּ֣י הָלַ֔ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר הָֽפַךְ־ אִ֛ישׁ מֵעַ֥ל מֶרְכַּבְתּ֖וֹ לִקְרָאתֶ֑ךָ הַעֵ֞ת לָקַ֤חַת אֶת־ הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ וְלָקַ֣חַת בְּגָדִ֔ים וְזֵיתִ֤ים וּכְרָמִים֙ וְצֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר וַעֲבָדִ֖ים וּשְׁפָחֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Therefore, the leprosy of Naaman will cling to you and your descendants forever!” And as Gehazi left his presence, he was leprous—as white as snow.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Gehazi was Elisha’s servant.
Elisha spoke to Gehazi.
Elisha said, “The leprosy that was on Naaman will cling to you.
It will also cling to your descendants.
This will last forever.”
Gehazi left Elisha’s presence.
Gehazi was leprous.
His skin was as white as snow.
passages.original: וְצָרַ֤עַת נַֽעֲמָן֙ תִּֽדְבַּק־ בְּךָ֔ וּֽבְזַרְעֲךָ לְעוֹלָ֑ם וַיֵּצֵ֥א מִלְּפָנָ֖יו מְצֹרָ֥ע כַּשָּֽׁלֶג׃ס
